title: The US is racing to fix its missile production challenge. Will it work, and can partners help? - Breaking Defense
html:
With global demand for missiles and missile defense surging, the US finds itself struggling to produce enough equipment to meet the Pentagon’s requirement — let alone that of foreign partners who rely on American systems. While there are efforts underway to increase production, there are still questions about whether its enough to help industry move as fast as needed.

In the latest edition of our look at missiles and missile defenses, Becca Wasser of Bloomberg Economics and Mark Cancian of the Center for International and Strategic Studies joined Breaking Defense Editor-in-Chief Aaron Mehta to discuss production challenges and the scary potential outcomes if the US and its partners can’t solve them.

Keep an eye on future episodes here. You can catch part one here, and part two here.
summary: Global demand for missiles and missile defense means production can't keep up. The Breaking Defense roundtable debates the way forward.
